children: Stocks in the U.A.E. lead gains across major Gulf markets as the country's non-oil private sector expanded at its strongest pace since late 2024. Capital Economics says the latest S&P Global PMI data point to a notable recovery in the U.A.E., with the headline index rising to 55.3 in August from 52.7 in July. It also points to a meaningful pickup in Dubai's travel-and-tourism sector for the first time since the war began, alongside sharp increases in construction and retail activity. The research firm says the broader Gulf PMI readings are encouraging given the U.S.-Iran tensions prevailing during the month. The Dubai Financial Market General Index rises 0.5%, Abu Dhabi's benchmark index gains 0.2%, Saudi Arabia's Tadawul All Share Index adds 0.2% and Qatar's QE Index rises 0.1%. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)
